NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under City Council Meeting agendas at rhe.city and during regular
  business hours in the office of the City Clerk. Meetings are live broadcast on the City's website and a
  recording is available for viewing after each meeting. Meetings are also broadcast on PVP-TV Channel 35
  (Cox) and Channel 39 (Verizon).

  Public Comment is welcome in-person on any item during City Council consideration of the item. Public
  correspondence may also be emailed to the City Clerk at laurenp@rollinghillsestates.gov. Emails

  consideration and included as part of the record. Members of the public may also comment online using
  eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos” page of the City’s website
  (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there will be an “eComment” button next
  to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to the City’s SpeakUp page. After you
  register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda. These comments can be seen by the
  public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the record.

  An opportunity is also provided for the public to comment on non-agenda items concerning City matters. If
  you would like to address the City Council regarding an item on this agenda or make a general public

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  APRIL 11, 2023

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
by MAYOR HUFF at 7:01 p.m. in the Council Chambers of City Hall.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by Los Angeles County Sheriff Deputy Daniel Okamoto.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Public Works Director David Wahba
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas
  Community Services Coordinator Matt Morrrow

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  RECOGNITION OF SHERIFF DEPUTY OKAMOTO

MAYOR HUFF presented Sheriff Deputy Okamoto with a Certificate of Recognition.

B.  PROCLAMATION DECLARING APRIL AS DMV/DONATE LIFE MONTH

MAYOR HUFF declared April as DMV/Donate Life Month.

C.  PROCLAMATION DECLARING APRIL AS EARTHQUAKE PREPAREDNESS MONTH

MAYOR HUFF declared April as Earthquake Preparedness Month.

D.  PROCLAMATION DECLARING APRIL 24, 2023 AS A "DAY OF REMEMBRANCE" OF
  THE ARMENIAN GENOCIDE OF 1915 - 1923

MAYOR HUFF declared April 24, 2023 as a “Day of Remembrance” of the Armenian Genocide
of 1915 – 1923, and COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN spoke about the history of the
Armenian Genocide and the importance of this day of remembrance.

Public comment was received from Taleen Tertzakian.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of the City
Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior to the
roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ,
  TO APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 4A-F AS FOLLOWS BY THE
  FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

APRIL 11, 2023
   APPROVED.

  APPROVED WARRANTS 66113 THROUGH 66144 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $114,724.95, AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 030623 THROUGH
  030723 IN THE AMOUNT OF $92,316.06 FOR A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ACTION ITEM: PORTUGUESE BEND
  HORSE SHOW REQUEST FOR ARENA #2 RENOVATION

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the renovation of Arena #2 at Ernie
  Howlett Park in the total amount of $123,272, for a City cost of $61,636.

Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas provided a staff report (as per the agenda material.)

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
Public testimony was received from Portuguese Bend Horse Show Chair Carol Rowe.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA stated that she feels it is important to attract world class riders
to the City, which puts Rolling Hills Estates on the map and reinforces the rural character of the
City.

COUNCIL MEMBER SHACHTER emphasized how important these horse shows are to the
community.

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE THE RENOVATION OF ARENA #2 AT ERNIE HOWLETT PARK IN
  THE TOTAL AMOUNT OF $123,272, FOR A CITY COST OF $61,636.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
APRIL 11, 2023
   AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None
B.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ACTION ITEM: SPORTS FIELD USE POLICY

  Recommendation: That the City Council review and approve the proposed Sports
  Field Use Policy.

Community Services Coordinator Matt Morrow provided a staff report (as per the agenda
material.)

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN spoke about the importance of keeping public parks public.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA expressed concern about setting limits on what groups can
charge for private sports clinics and stated that she could not support the policy as written.

Assistant City Manager Davis highlighted some of the challenges the City has faced with youth
sports leagues over the past few years, noting that private coaching has taken away from some
of the public programming.

MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ confirmed that groups A, B, C and D have priority in that order.
Community Services Coordinator Morrow explained how the use of fields would be allocated
within each group. MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ requested the allocation process be
delineated within the policy. Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas added that in-season
sports also get priority over other sports.

MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ inquired how the policy works with groups that have contracts
with the City. Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas explained that the policy will work in
tandem with any contracts made with specific groups.

Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas confirmed that all contracts held by various groups
for field use would not conflict with the proposed policy, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER
STEGURA.

Assistant City Manager Davis explained that penalties are incorporated into the policy, which
do not exist now for the groups not complying with City rules, in response to COUNCIL
MEMBER STEGURA.

City Manager Grammer suggested a City Council Subcommittee to refine the policy and bring
back to the City Council at a future date.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA stated she would like to see no cap on the cost of clinics, and
suggested the policy be more explicit by putting private contractors lower on the priority list.

Further discussion ensued about concerns about the policy as written.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
Public testimony was received by Lou Persichina, Park and Activities Commissioner.

  CONSENSUS TO CREATE A SUBCOMMITTEE INCLUDING COUNCIL
  MEMBER STEGURA AND MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ TO WORK WITH THE
  CURRENT YOUTH SPORTS SUBCOMMITTEE AND STAFF TO REVISE THE
  SPORTS FIELD USE POLICY AND RETURN TO COUNCIL AT A FUTURE
  DATE.

MAYOR HUFF so ordered.

C.  NAMING OF FUTURE PARK SITE LOCATED AT THE NORTHEAST CORNER OF
  PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH AND PALOS VERDES DRIVE EAST

  Recommendation: That the City Council select “Founders Park” as the name for the
  future park site located at the northeast corner of Palos Verdes Drive North and Palos
  Verdes Drive East and direct staff to install a plaque acknowledging the City’s
  founders at the future park.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
APRIL 11, 2023
 Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas provided a staff report (as per the agenda material.)
Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  ZERUNYAN, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  SELECT “FOUNDERS PARK” AS THE NAME FOR THE FUTURE PARK SITE
  LOCATED AT THE NORTHEAST CORNER OF PALOS VERDES DRIVE
  NORTH AND PALOS VERDES DRIVE EAST AND DIRECT STAFF TO
  INSTALL A PLAQUE ACKNOWLEDGING THE CITY’S FOUNDERS AT THE
  FUTURE PARK.

MAYOR HUFF so ordered.

D.  PARK PROJECT-AUTHORIZATION TO SOLICIT BIDS

  Recommendation: That the City Council authorize staff to solicit bids for the
  construction of a new park at the northeast corner of Palos Verdes Drive North and
  Palos Verdes Drive East, with a sealed bid opening date of Thursday, May 25, 2023,
  all to the satisfaction of the City Attorney.

Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the agenda material.)

City Attorney Davis explained that public works contracts typically involve a sealed bid process,
in response to COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM
  SCHMITZ, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AUTHORIZE STAFF TO SOLICIT BIDS FOR THE CONSTRUCTION OF
  FOUNDERS PARK AT THE NORTHEAST CORNER OF PALOS VERDES
  DRIVE NORTH AND PALOS VERDES DRIVE EAST, WITH A SEALED BID
  OPENING DATE OF THURSDAY, MAY 25, 2023, ALL TO THE
  SATISFACTION OF THE CITY ATTORNEY.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

E.  LETTER IN OPPOSITION TO SB 423 (WIENER) - LAND USE: STREAMLINED
  HOUSING APPROVALS: MULTIFAMILY HOUSING DEVELOPMENTS

  Recommendation: That the City Council authorize the Mayor to sign the attached letter
  in opposition to SB 423 (Wiener).

City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per the agenda material.)

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA suggested the second paragraph be deleted.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN suggested “housing crisis” be called “affordability crisis.”

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
Public testimony was received from John Owens and Lynn Yen.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
APRIL 11, 2023
   AUTHORIZE THE MAYOR TO SIGN THE LETTER IN OPPOSITION TO SB
  423 (WIENER), AS AMENDED.

MAYOR HUFF so ordered.

9.  OLD BUSINESS

None.

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

None.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA attended the Clean Power Alliance Board meeting last
week.

MAYOR HUFF reported that she and COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA attended the ribbon
cutting for the Teen Annex at the Library, and MAYOR HUFF will be attending the Cal Cities
City Leaders Summit in Sacramento this weekend.

At 8:13 PM MAYOR HUFF adjourned the City Council meeting in memory of Los Angeles
